capture.final_message:
View the theorem as a conjunction of two independent standard facts.

For the first part, identify `Nat.factoredNumbers s` with exponent vectors on the finite set of primes in `s`. Multiplicativity gives
\[
f\!\left(\prod_p p^{e_p}\right)=\prod_p f(p)^{e_p}.
\]
Thus the sum becomes a finite product of geometric series. The hypothesis \(\|f(p)\|<1\) makes each series absolutely summable, yielding both summability of the norms and
\[
\sum_{m\in\mathrm{factoredNumbers}(s)}f(m)
 =\prod_{\substack{p\in s\\p\ \mathrm{prime}}}(1-f(p))^{-1}.
\]

For the equivalence, prove both propositions independently:

- The left side is the Möbius-inversion formula
  \[
  \Phi_n(X)=\prod_{de=n}(X^e-1)^{\mu(d)}.
  \]
  Start from \(X^n-1=\prod_{d\mid n}\Phi_d(X)\), apply multiplicative Möbius inversion, and work in `RatFunc R` so negative Möbius exponents are meaningful. `IsDomain R` supplies the required fraction-field embedding.

- The right side follows by unfolding `toArithmeticFunction`: away from zero, its value is exactly the original function \(n\mapsto\chi(n)\). The assumption `hn : n ≠ 0` is essential because the construction separately forces the value at zero to be zero.

Once both universal statements are available, form the `Iff` by ignoring either implication’s hypothesis and invoking the independently proved opposite statement.
